external_relations.target_title: bug: make global-skill validation cleanup transactional and non-destructive

source.description:
## PROBLEM
Security audit for xtrm-qs9in found that concurrent same-user `xt update --apply`, install, or bootstrap processes can race while reading stale manifests, creating independent backups, mutating ~/.xtrm/skills, and performing process-local rollback. Atomic directory placement does not serialize the wider transaction.

## SUCCESS
All mutations of the shared global skill root are serialized across processes. Concurrent commands either wait safely or fail with a bounded actionable diagnostic. Final tree, manifest, state, and backup lineage are consistent.

## SCOPE
Global skill bootstrap/update/install mutation boundary, cross-process lock lifecycle, crash/stale-lock recovery, diagnostics, and isolated-HOME concurrency regressions.

## NON_GOALS
No change to skill precedence or package contents. No real-HOME mutation in tests.

## CONSTRAINTS
Reuse a proven repository lock primitive if one exists. Lock the complete read-backup-mutate-state-write/rollback transaction. Fail closed on unverifiable stale lock ownership. Preserve user/unmanaged state. No new dependency unless required.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Two concurrent sandbox-HOME updates serialize.
- [ ] Crash/stale lock recovery is deterministic.
- [ ] Manifest/state/tree stay consistent.
- [ ] Timeout/error diagnostics are bounded and path-safe.
- [ ] Reviewer and security PASS.

## OUTPUT
Implementation, isolated concurrency proof, GitNexus impact/change report, and audit verdicts.
source.title: bug: serialize concurrent global-skill mutations
